tool_analysis:
1) Step Analysis:
The recorded session performs a complete Magento Admin orders export flow:
- Navigates directly to the Sales > Orders admin URL.
- Encounters the login screen and authenticates using username and password fields labeled "User Name" and "Password", then clicks the "Log in" button.
- Arrives at the Sales > Orders grid.
- Closes an "Incoming Message" popup that can overlap controls.
- Applies a filter on the Order # column via the filter row and clicks the Search button to narrow the grid to a specific order.
- Uses the "Export to" dropdown to choose an export format (Excel XML in the demo) and clicks the "Export" button, which triggers a download URL for the filtered grid.

2) Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given Magento admin credentials, an optional order number filter, and an export format (CSV or Excel XML), will:
- Navigate to the Sales > Orders grid
- Log in if required
- Optionally filter by Order #
- Export the (filtered or unfiltered) orders grid in the requested format

3) Action Plan:
1. Navigate to the Magento Sales > Orders admin URL.
2. Perform login on the Magento Admin login page using robust interactions (index/elementHash for the username, password fields, and login button) to avoid brittle CSS selector failures noted previously.
3. After login, ensure we are on the Sales > Orders grid URL.
4. Close the "Incoming Message" popup via its close link (elementHash-based) to prevent interference with toolbar controls.
5. If an order increment ID filter is provided, input it into the Order # filter field in the filter row and click the Search button.
6. Change the export format in the "Export to" dropdown to the requested format (CSV or Excel XML).
7. Click the Export button to initiate the export of the current grid (respecting filters).

4) Variable Identification:
Based on the steps and site structure, the key inputs are:
- "username": text typed into the User Name field ("admin" in the demo). Required for login.
- "password": text typed into the Password field ("password123" in the demo). Required for login.
- "order_increment_id": text typed into the Order # filter input ("000000299" in the demo). Optional; when omitted, the full grid (current filters) is exported.
- "export_format": visible text selected in the Export dropdown: either "CSV" or "Excel XML". Required because the tool’s purpose is to choose the desired machine-readable format.

No URL-parameter manipulation pattern for export was demonstrated; the export is triggered via the standard grid select+button controls (POST or JavaScript-driven link), so interaction is required rather than a single URL navigation.

5) Step Optimization & Selector Strategy:
- The previous failed tool used a brittle CSS selector for the username field (input[name="login[username]"][type="text"]). The current session shows that interacting via index/elementHash works reliably on this Magento instance.
- For robustness and determinism, we will use the recorded elementHash values for critical inputs and buttons (username, password, login, popup close, Order # filter, Search, export format select, Export) in deterministic interaction steps instead of fragile textual CSS selectors.
- We will not add extra filtering, sorting, or pagination beyond the demonstrated Order # filter, in line with the single-purpose requirement.
- Navigation is done with a single direct URL to the Sales > Orders page; Magento automatically redirects unauthenticated users to login and then back to the grid after authentication, so no extra navigation hops are necessary.
- No additional extraction steps are needed in the tool itself; the goal is to perform the export, not to read data back from the page.

Because export and login require UI form submissions (likely POST), URL-parameter optimization is not appropriate here, so we preserve the interactive flow.
name: tool_export_orders_v2
description: Logs into Magento Admin and exports the current (optionally filtered) Sales > Orders grid to CSV or Excel XML.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Sales > Orders grid URL (will redirect to login if not authenticated).
Enter the Magento Admin username into the 'User Name' field on the login page.
Enter the Magento Admin password into the 'Password' field on the login page.
Click the 'Log in' button to submit the Magento Admin login form.
Wait for the Magento Admin to authenticate and load the Sales > Orders grid page.
Close the 'Incoming Message' notification popup so that it does not obscure grid controls.
If an order_increment_id was provided, type it into the 'Order #' filter input in the orders grid filter row. If empty, this effectively leaves the filter unchanged.
Click the 'Search' button to apply the current filters (including the Order # if provided).
Wait for the grid to refresh and display the filtered orders list.
In the 'Export to' dropdown, choose the desired export format (CSV or Excel XML).
Click the 'Export' button to initiate download of the current (optionally filtered) orders grid in the selected format.

input_schema.name: username
input_schema.description: Magento Admin username to log into the backend (e.g., 'admin').

input_schema.name: password
input_schema.description: Magento Admin password corresponding to the username (e.g., 'password123').

input_schema.name: order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Optional Order # (increment ID) to filter the Sales > Orders grid before export, e.g., '000000299'. Leave empty to export the current unfiltered grid.

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Visible label of the export format to use from the 'Export to' dropdown. Must be either 'CSV' or 'Excel XML'.
